```python core.CCModel( variable_name, state_variables=None, non_integrated_state_vars=None, diagnostic_variables=None, ) ``` The overarching model structure for ClimateCritters. CCModel serves as the archetype/parent class for models within the ``model_critters`` directory. It is not meant to be instantiated directly. ## Parameter handling {.doc-section .doc-section-parameter-handling} Models may define a ``param_values`` dict that maps parameter names to constants, callables, or ``Forcing`` objects. Use ``get_param_value(name, t, state)`` inside ``dydt`` to resolve any of these uniformly. To make a parameter state- or time-dependent after construction, assign a callable via ``set_param_value``:: model.set_param_value('rho', lambda t, state: 28.0 + 0.1 * state[0]) To replace a *computation method* (e.g. ``calc_albedo``) on a single instance without subclassing, use ``set_function``. ## External forcings {.doc-section .doc-section-external-forcings} Use ``register_forcing`` to attach a time-varying external driver to any named parameter or state variable after construction:: model.register_forcing('S0', forcing_obj) # parameter model.register_forcing('x', forcing_obj, 'additive', timing='pre') # state See ``register_forcing`` for the full contract and default timing rules. ## Methods | Name | Description | | --- | --- | | [clear_forcings](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.clear_forcings) | Remove registered forcings. | | [doc](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.doc) | Pretty-print documentation for the requested category. | | [dydt](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.dydt) | Define the system of differential equations. | | [get_forcings](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.get_forcings) | Return registered forcings, optionally filtered by variable name. | | [get_param_value](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.get_param_value) | Resolve a named parameter to its value at the current time and state. | | [get_param_vector](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.get_param_vector) | Resolve a parameter and broadcast it to a fixed-length vector. | | [integrate](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.integrate) | Integrate the model over a time span and return a :class:`CCOutput`. | | [list](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.list) | Return a list of names for the requested category. | | [populate_diagnostics_from_history](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.populate_diagnostics_from_history) | Compute diagnostic variables from the full solved trajectory. | | [post_integrate](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.post_integrate) | Orchestrate post-solve output construction for ``uses_post_history`` models. | | [register_forcing](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.register_forcing) | Attach an external forcing to a named parameter or state variable. | | [set_function](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.set_function) | Swap out a model calculation function on a single instance. | | [set_param_value](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.set_param_value) | Add or update a parameter and keep the attribute and ``param_values`` in sync. | | [validate_initial_state](#climatecritters.core.CCModel.validate_initial_state) | Validate and normalize the initial state vector. | ### clear_forcings { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.clear_forcings } ```python core.CCModel.clear_forcings(var_name=None) ``` Remove registered forcings. #### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} [**var_name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : If given, clear only the forcings for that variable. If omitted, clear all forcings on the model. ### doc { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.doc } ```python core.CCModel.doc(print_target) ``` Pretty-print documentation for the requested category. Descriptions are parsed from the NumPy-style docstrings of the class and its base classes. For parameters the current value is also shown. #### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} [**print_target**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [([state_variables](`climatecritters.core.ccmodel.CCModel.state_variables`), [parameters](`parameters`), [diagnostic_variables](`climatecritters.core.ccmodel.CCModel.diagnostic_variables`))]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'state_variables\']{.parameter-default} : The category to document. ### dydt { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.dydt } ```python core.CCModel.dydt(t, y) ``` Define the system of differential equations. Must be overridden by every subclass. The solver calls this at each timestep with the current time ``t`` and state vector ``y``, and expects a list of derivatives of the same length as ``y``. Use ``get_param`` inside the implementation to access parameters. ### get_forcings { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.get_forcings } ```python core.CCModel.get_forcings(var_name=None) ``` Return registered forcings, optionally filtered by variable name. #### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} [**var_name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : If given, return the list of ``ForcingSpec`` objects for that variable. If omitted, return the full ``_forcings`` dict. ### get_param_value { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.get_param_value } ```python core.CCModel.get_param_value(name, t, state) ``` Resolve a named parameter to its value at the current time and state. This is the standard way to access parameters inside ``dydt``. It looks up the value from ``param_values`` by name and delegates resolution to ``_resolve_param``, so callers in ``dydt`` don't need to know whether a parameter is stored as a constant, a callable, or a Forcing object. ### get_param_vector { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.get_param_vector } ```python core.CCModel.get_param_vector(name, t, state, size) ``` Resolve a parameter and broadcast it to a fixed-length vector. Spatial models often allow parameters to be either a single scalar (applied uniformly) or a full grid-length array. This method resolves the parameter via ``get_param`` and then either broadcasts a scalar or validates that an array has the expected size, eliminating that boilerplate from every ``dydt`` that works on a spatial grid. ### integrate { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.integrate } ```python core.CCModel.integrate( t_span=None, y0=None, method='RK45', dt=None, output_time=None, run_name=None, kwargs=None, ) ``` Integrate the model over a time span and return a :class:`CCOutput`. #### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} [**t_span**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple of float]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : ``(t0, tf)`` integration bounds for the solver. [**y0**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[array](`array`) - [like](`like`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : Initial conditions. Length must match the number of integrated state variables. [**method**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'RK45\']{.parameter-default} : Solver to use: ``'RK45'`` (default), ``'euler'``, ``'euler_maruyama'``, ``'heun_maruyama'``, ``'milstein'``, ``'rk4'``, or any method accepted by ``scipy.integrate.solve_ivp``. SDE solver guidance: * ``'euler_maruyama'`` — strong order 0.5; baseline stochastic. * ``'heun_maruyama'`` — strong order 1.0 for additive noise (diffusion independent of state); preferred for models like Melcher et al. (2025). * ``'milstein'`` — strong order 1.0 for multiplicative noise (diffusion depends on state); uses a finite-difference approximation of ``∂g/∂y``, so no analytical Jacobian is required. [**dt**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[float](`float`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : Fixed timestep for ``euler``, ``euler_maruyama``, and ``rk4``. Required for those methods. [**output_time**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[array](`array`) - [like](`like`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : If provided, the returned ``CCOutput`` is immediately reframed onto this time axis (e.g. to exclude a spin-up period). ``output.model_time`` always retains the raw solver grid. [**run_name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : Label stored on the output. Defaults to ``', dt=
'``. [**kwargs**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[dict](`dict`)]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : Additional solver options. For ``solve_ivp`` methods these are forwarded directly (e.g. ``rtol``, ``atol``, ``t_eval``). For ``euler_maruyama``, ``random_seed`` is extracted here. For ``rk4``, ``si`` (sampling interval) is extracted here. .. deprecated:: Passing ``dt`` inside ``kwargs`` is deprecated. Use the explicit ``dt`` parameter instead. ### list { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.list } ```python core.CCModel.list(list_target) ``` Return a list of names for the requested category. #### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} [**list_target**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [([state_variables](`climatecritters.core.ccmodel.CCModel.state_variables`), [parameters](`parameters`), [diagnostic_variables](`climatecritters.core.ccmodel.CCModel.diagnostic_variables`))]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\'state_variables\']{.parameter-default} : The category to enumerate. #### Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns} [**names**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [list of str]{.parameter-annotation} : ### populate_diagnostics_from_history { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.populate_diagnostics_from_history } ```python core.CCModel.populate_diagnostics_from_history(time, history) ``` Compute diagnostic variables from the full solved trajectory. Called by ``post_integrate`` for models where ``uses_post_history = True``. The base implementation does nothing because diagnostics are model-specific; subclasses override this to derive any quantities that can only be computed once the complete trajectory is available (e.g. derived fields, fluxes). ### post_integrate { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.post_integrate } ```python core.CCModel.post_integrate(time, history) ``` Orchestrate post-solve output construction for ``uses_post_history`` models. Some models (e.g. spatial PDEs) cannot accumulate state during the solve without side effects; instead they store the full trajectory and derive all outputs here. This method sequences the required steps in the correct order: build the structured state array, set the time axis, populate diagnostics, and convert diagnostic lists to arrays. It is called automatically by ``integrate`` when ``uses_post_history = True``. ### register_forcing { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.register_forcing } ```python core.CCModel.register_forcing( var_name, forcing_object, attachment_style=None, timing=None, ) ``` Attach an external forcing to a named parameter or state variable. #### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} [**var_name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} : Name of the target. Must exist in ``param_values`` (parameter namespace) or ``state_variables_names`` (state namespace). If the name appears in both, a ``ValueError`` is raised — this is a model design issue worth resolving explicitly. [**forcing_object**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} []{.parameter-annotation} : A ``Forcing`` instance, a callable ``f(t)`` → scalar/array, or any object with a ``get_forcing(t)`` method. [**attachment_style**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [([replacement](`replacement`), [additive](`additive`))]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\"replacement\"]{.parameter-default} : How the forcing value is applied. * Parameters default to ``"replacement"``. ``"additive"`` is also supported and adds the forcing value to the nominal parameter at each step (e.g. ``k = k_0 + ε(t)``). * State variables have **no default** — ``attachment_style`` is required. This is intentional: injecting into a live state variable is a significant physical choice that should be explicit. [**timing**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [([pre](`pre`), [post](`post`))]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [\"pre\"]{.parameter-default} : When the forcing is applied relative to the integration step. Derived automatically in most cases: * parameter + any style → ``"pre"`` (always; no override) * state + replacement → ``"post"`` (always; warns if ``"pre"`` passed) * state + additive → **required**; raise if not provided #### Raises {.doc-section .doc-section-raises} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[ValueError](`ValueError`)]{.parameter-annotation} : If ``var_name`` is not found, if ``attachment_style`` is missing for a state variable, if ``timing`` is missing for state + additive, or if a second ``"replacement"`` is registered on the same variable. ### set_function { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.set_function } ```python core.CCModel.set_function(name, function, bind=None) ``` Swap out a model calculation function on a single instance. Subclassing is the right approach when a different formulation should apply everywhere, but for one-off experiments (e.g. testing an alternative albedo scheme without writing a new class) it is useful to replace a single method on one instance. The ``bind`` parameter handles whether the replacement expects ``self`` as its first argument. #### Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters} [**name**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation} : Name of an existing callable attribute (e.g., ``calc_k``). [**function**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[callable](`callable`)]{.parameter-annotation} : Replacement callable. [**bind**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[bool](`bool`) or None]{.parameter-annotation} [ = ]{.parameter-default-sep} [None]{.parameter-default} : ``True``: bind as instance method (expects ``self`` as first arg). ``False``: assign as a plain callable. ``None``: infer from whether the first argument is named ``self`` or ``model``. ### set_param_value { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.set_param_value } ```python core.CCModel.set_param_value(name, value) ``` Add or update a parameter and keep the attribute and ``param_values`` in sync. ``__setattr__`` syncs the direction ``model.alpha = v → param_values``, but only for names already in ``param_values``. This method handles the reverse and covers inserting new parameters that weren't declared at initialization. ### validate_initial_state { #climatecritters.core.CCModel.validate_initial_state } ```python core.CCModel.validate_initial_state(y0) ``` Validate and normalize the initial state vector. Exists as a method so that subclasses with non-standard initial state requirements (e.g. a spatially discretised model that accepts a scalar and broadcasts it to the grid) can override it. The base implementation delegates to the utility in ``utils/solver``.
